Subject: Cross-border evacuation matrix + BGP tie-break — EU/APAC private deploys

Team / Finnix folks —

Thanks for the quick sync yesterday. We need to lock the operational plan and the network tie-break rules for the EU/APAC private deployment before we schedule the cutover window. High level asks:

- Confirm legal/data-residency constraints in the Finnish and Singapore contracts (RPO/RTO ceilings).
- Agree an L3 evacuation matrix that specifies: when to fail traffic to warm-standby region, how to drain KV caches safely, and which KMS keys are allowed to cross-region for emergency reads.
- Define a deterministic BGP tie-break / local-preference plan so traffic doesn't flap across regions during partial outages.

I've attached a first-pass evacuation matrix and a diagram for the BGP tie-break suggestion (local-pref + prepend rules). Please review the specifics in tab "Trigger Conditions".

Key constraints to bear in mind:
- EU customers: strict egress gating for some datasets; no persistent cross-border writes without process sign-off.
- APAC site: hot-standby for inference only (no persistent primary custody of logs).
- KMS policy: only read-only emergency access across boundaries, auditable via CloudHSM key policy.

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) Finnix to confirm contractual holdbacks and whether temporary cross-region reads require DPA amendment (Tom).
2) Karthik to produce a short L3 runbook with the exact BGP local-pref values and prepends (we'll need exact prefixes).
3) Laura to schedule a tabletop on Oct 15 to validate the drills and authorization chain.

I'll host a follow-up review on Monday to go through comments.

Attachments: evacuation-matrix-v1.xlsx (matrix + trigger table), bgp-tiebreak-diagram.png

Thanks,
Vivek
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Vivek —

Thanks for the write-up and the artifacts. A few clarifying items from our side: 

- Contract/data-residency: We have a standard regional DPA that prohibits writes outside the EU for a subset of telemetry. Reads for emergency troubleshooting are allowed with an audit trail. I will share the specific clause by EOD.
- RPO/RTO expectations: Our security team needs RTO <= 15m and RPO <= 5m for the EU inference tenant to accept any cross-region fallback for reads. Is that achievable with your KV cache drain approach?
- Peering: We can provide the advertised prefixes; however, the vendor circuits on the APAC side are metered — aggressive path-flipping will cost us and may violate peering agreements. We need a deterministic tie-break approach that avoids oscillation.

Questions:
1) For the KMS emergency-read plan — will Redwood use a restricted KMS role that only allows decrypt for a named session ID and logs to our audit endpoint?
2) Can you confirm whether the warm-standby will accept writes under any circumstance (we assume no).

We're ok to proceed with the tabletop on Oct 15; please send the invite.

—Tom
Tom Liu
SRE Lead, Finnix Logistics

Subject: Re: Cross-border evacuation matrix + BGP tie-break — technical notes (L3 runbook draft)

Tom / Vivek / team —

Quick technical notes and actions (draft L3 runbook attached):

- BGP tie-break: propose local-preference ordering:
  100 -> local-region primary (no prepends)
  90  -> warm-standby region (2x AS-path prepend on warm-standby advertisement)
  80  -> internet fallback via transit (blackhole guarded)

  Rationale: explicit local-pref prevents path-swapping on transient circuit flaps; prepend reduces attractivity of standby without blackholing it.

- Trigger table (short):
  - Partial AZ transient (<5m): do not change prefixes; rely on infra-level failover.
  - Regional control-plane outage (>10m) with telemetry gap: promote warm-standby for read-only traffic after manual auth (Escalation group A).
  - Data-sensitivity flag = HIGH -> no cross-region read allowed.

- Cache drain: we will attempt non-blocking read-while-drain to ensure RTO target. If we cannot meet RTO <= 15m for EU, we fall back to read-only fallback API that hits live datastore in-region (slower).

- KMS: implement session-scoped decrypt role (limited TTL, auditable). Tech note: Redwood will call Finnix audit endpoint with session metadata; Finnix must provide the HTTP ingest endpoint and shared cert.

Action items:
- Karthik: collect exact /24 prefixes for BGP adverts from Finnix (Tom).
- Laura: confirm legal gating list of datasets.
- Marissa: coordinate tabletop invite and prep list.

Attachment: l3-runbook-draft.md

Karthik
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
